tagline: Keep the data moving — the routers, switches, firewalls, and Wi-Fi that connect everything.
what_you_do: You install, configure, and maintain the network that a business runs on. Day to day you watch for outages, trace connectivity problems one hop at a time, configure switches and routers, manage IP addressing and VLANs, and keep firewalls and Wi-Fi healthy. Entry work often starts in a Network Operations Center (NOC), watching dashboards and triaging incidents before they spread.
day_in_life: Check overnight alerts and the monitoring dashboard for anything degraded
Trace a 'the internet is slow in Building C' complaint down to a single switch port or uplink
Configure a new VLAN and update firewall rules for a team that's moving offices
Document the fix in the runbook so the next person can repeat it
Escalate a hardware failure and coordinate the swap with the vendor

salary.growth: Steady — the NOC is a well-known launchpad
salary.note: U.S. BLS figure for Computer Network Support Specialists (15-1231); a median is the midpoint of everyone employed, so entry pay runs lower. Verify against the live BLS page before deciding.

downsides: NOCs run 24/7, so nights, weekends, and on-call pages are normal early on. Alarm fatigue is real, and you can get blamed for outages outside your control. The ladder is slow without certs.

fits_if: You're curious about what makes a network fast or slow
You're okay with shift work and being the person who fixes things
less_ideal_if: You'd rather build new things than keep systems running
You want to avoid deep technical detail

skills.name: TCP/IP & subnetting fundamentals
skills.note: The bedrock — how addresses, routes, and ports actually work.

skills.name: Structured troubleshooting & packet capture
skills.note: Isolate faults tier by tier; read a Wireshark trace.

skills.name: Network automation (Python/Ansible)
skills.note: A force-multiplier that raises pay and mobility.

certs.title: Cisco CCST Networking
certs.reason: The $125 confidence checkpoint with free official training — for students and budget starts; committed adults can go straight to Network+/CCNA.

certs.title: CompTIA Network+
certs.reason: Vendor-neutral proof of networking fundamentals — the recognized entry signal.

certs.title: Cisco CCNA
certs.reason: The strong hands-on networking cert; opens more doors and pay once you have the fundamentals.

certs.title: Juniper JNCIA-Junos
certs.reason: The Juniper-side equivalent of CCNA — free official training and deep-discount vouchers make it the cheapest legit routing & switching cert; strong in ISP and service-provider shops.

certs.title: CCNP Enterprise
certs.reason: Where senior network roles start — ENCOR + a concentration, once CCNA-level work is second nature.

certs.title: CCNP Automation
certs.reason: The NetDevOps professional tier — if the Python/Ansible direction from stage 4 becomes your lane, this is its credential.

trial.objective: See how packets actually travel and what a NOC watches all day, using commands already on your computer.
trial.disclosure: Built-in commands only; optional free Cisco Packet Tracer or Wireshark for a deeper follow-up.

roadmap.title: Learn the fundamentals
roadmap.focus: TCP/IP, subnetting, switching, VLANs — free via Professor Messer / Cisco Networking Academy. Build a home lab in Packet Tracer.

roadmap.title: Prove networking fundamentals
roadmap.focus: Earn CompTIA Network+ to get past resume filters for NOC and network support roles.

roadmap.title: Go hands-on with real gear
roadmap.focus: Study Cisco CCNA — routing, OSPF, ACLs, WAN — and lab everything. This is where you become employable as a network engineer.

roadmap.title: Specialize and go professional
roadmap.focus: Pick a direction — network security, cloud networking, or automation (Python/Ansible) — then formalize it with CCNP Enterprise (ENCOR + a concentration) when senior roles are the target.

adjacent_paths.reason: Networking knowledge is a direct feeder into security operations.
Cloud networking is a natural next step as infrastructure moves to the cloud.
